llm.summary: The shock today is credit, not rates: investors are dumping data-centre bonds as AI borrowers hit what the FT calls a 'Darwin moment,' neocloud paper is blowing up, and global chip stocks are sinking on financing fears rather than demand fears. Treasury yields fell hard — 10-year back below 5.11% — but for the wrong reason, a flight to safety out of the tech rout, even as September PPI printed +6.3% y/y, the hottest since 2022, and retail sales beat on gasoline. Brokerages have pushed the next Fed move to a December HIKE, so duration relief today is a risk signal, not an easing signal. The fundamental side of AI keeps confirming: TSMC posted record profit, ASML said its capacity plan falls short of demand with order visibility into 2029-30 — and both were sold anyway, the clearest sign yet that the market is repricing who pays for the capex rather than whether the capex happens. The gaps tell the story better than the indices: FIX -7.4%, EME -4.3%, LRCX -6.0%, BE -7.6% — the data-centre build-out supply chain is being marked down, while NVR gapped +4.3% on lower yields. Gold reversed yesterday's slide as the dollar softened, restoring the hedge bid that looked broken 24 hours ago. Memory narrative flipped again — from Chinese-breakthrough scarcity panic to 2029 oversupply fear — which mechanically improves the BOM outlook for our SMCI and HPQ positions even as SMCI's customer credit quality deteriorates. Regime is now a four-way coin flip with Stagflation (27.5, +8.9) and Reflation (26.1, +9.3) both rising and Goldilocks collapsing -8.1.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: the marginal seller is no longer a rates trader, it is a credit trader. Data-centre and neocloud bond spreads widening means the cost of financing AI capex has jumped, which hits the second derivative of order flow long before it hits reported revenue. That is why TSMC's record profit and ASML's sold-out capacity were both punished — the market is distinguishing between the rent collectors (ASML, TSMC, NVDA at the top) and the leveraged buyers (neoclouds, SMCI's customer base, contractors like FIX and EME). Expect continued compression in anything that funds growth with debt and anything whose backlog depends on a tier-2 cloud's ability to roll paper. Yields falling 10bps on a 6.3% PPI print is not a dovish signal; it is collateral rotation, and it will reverse violently if December hike odds harden. Near term I want cash flow that is already banked, pricing power in energy and power generation, and I want to be underweight the AI balance-sheet complex while staying long the AI income statement.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: stagflation-lite remains the modal path, now with a credit overlay. PPI at 6.3% is pipeline cost that either compresses margins or gets passed to a consumer who is already spending on gasoline rather than goods. Mortgage rates above 7% into 2027 freeze the housing transaction economy, Real Estate flows at -73 and Prologis trimming the outer edge of guidance say the logistics-REIT cycle has peaked for this rate regime. The AI capex cycle does not stop — ASML's 2029-30 visibility, Brookfield/NextEra's $100bn nuclear-site hub and PJM's data-centre registry are hard commitments — but the financing mix shifts from high-yield neocloud debt toward hyperscaler cash flow and utility ratebase. That transition is deflationary for AI-adjacent equity multiples and bullish for the regulated power, nuclear and gas-turbine complex, which gets paid regardless of who wins. Financials at -66 flows into a December hike is a mispricing worth watching: BlackRock's record $205bn inflows, General Atlantic's $10bn IPO, Anthropic's $16.8bn revenue pre-IPO and Cboe extending options hours all point to market-structure winners that thrive on volatility and asset accumulation, not on credit growth.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: three structural facts. First, the binding constraint on AI has migrated from chips to capital and electrons — whoever owns the interconnect, the ratebase and the uranium collects a toll for a decade, which is why Brookfield/NextEra repurposing a Cold War nuclear site and BWXT raising guidance matter more than any GPU benchmark. Second, we are watching the first real credit cycle of the AI era; a shakeout among leveraged compute intermediaries is healthy and will concentrate the industry into five or six balance sheets, exactly as happened in telecom after 2001 — the fibre still got used, the owners just changed. Third, the household is being structurally repriced: electricity search queries spiking on 'bill assistance' and 'bill calculator,' mortgage rates stuck above 7% into a third year, and open questioning of college as 'good debt' are all the same phenomenon — the shift from an asset-price economy to an income economy, where security and affordability beat aspiration, and where energy is a household budget line rather than a background utility. That permanently favours value retail, regulated power, essential health, and the firms that sell time and cost removal to businesses rather than growth to consumers.

short_term: Energy affordability is now a household-level stressor, not a macro abstraction — rising search for 'electricity bill assistance,' 'bill calculator' and 'average bill' alongside a gasoline-driven retail sales beat means the consumer is spending more to get the same, which is volume-negative for discretionary goods.

Investors are rotating to short-duration safety at the first sign of credit stress: Treasuries bid despite a 6.3% PPI, gold rebounding on a softer dollar, bitcoin tested $81,000 and failed — risk hedging is happening through government paper and metal, not crypto.

Firms are cutting discretionary spend defensively: big brands reducing advertising, Visa booking $563m of job-cut costs despite resilient consumer volumes, Albertsons withdrawing guidance, FMC and Pentair cutting outlooks — managements are pre-emptively protecting margin.

Security spend is being forced, not chosen — Bank of America hiring 1,000 contractors to patch flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos is the template: AI capability is creating non-discretionary remediation budgets, and cybersecurity now leads cloud and software in flows.

Households are relocating for family logistics ('baby chasers' reshaping regional housing) rather than for jobs or price appreciation, because the mortgage lock-in means moves must solve a life problem to be worth the rate reset.
Retail attention is clustering on access and utility — Starlink queries up 59%, stablecoin queries up 25% — people want connectivity and dollar-denominated settlement, not speculation.
long_term: Electricity becomes a status and security good: households that can self-generate or lock in rates separate from those exposed to data-centre-driven ratebase increases, creating a political economy fight that utilities, nuclear and gas will win commercially and lose reputationally.

Housing converts from an aspiration to an inheritance: with 7%+ mortgages persisting into 2027, transaction volumes stay structurally depressed, rental and multigenerational living normalise, and wealth formation shifts from property to income and securities.

The knowledge economy's price signal is breaking — open questioning of college as 'good debt' plus agentic AI compressing entry-level white-collar work pushes demand toward short-cycle, verifiable, AI-adjacent skills and toward employers who train.

AI moves from novelty to ambient infrastructure in the home (Amazon's Bee always-listening personal AI, local AI PCs like RTX Spark), which trades privacy for convenience and creates a durable second market in consumer data governance and edge inference silicon.

Capital markets democratise access to private AI compounders — Anthropic's pre-IPO $16.8bn revenue, General Atlantic's $10bn listing, Cboe's extended options hours — public investors will finally get exposure, usually late and at the wrong price.

Health shifts from episodic treatment to continuous measurement (CGM, longevity queries, faster-to-manufacture cancer vaccines per Merck), making device and diagnostics annuities more valuable than one-shot therapeutics.
